question_gloss: Question about compensation or restoration for damaged property or items.

rotation.source_passage:
but come to me, if ever before
you heard my far-off cries
and heeded, and came, leaving
your father's golden


house, yoking your chariot: beautiful
swift sparrows whirred on quick wings
and drew you down through the middle air
over the black earth


from heaven: they arrived in an instant;
and you, blessed one, a smile
on your immortal face, asked me
what was the matter now, and why


was I calling now, and what
did I most want to happen
in my maddened heart: "Who now
should Persuasion lead


back to your love? Who wrongs you,
Sappho? For even if she runs,
soon she will pursue; if she refuses
gifts, soon she will give them;
rotation.enantiomorph:
but fall to me, if ever once
you tracked my emptied channels
and answered, and descended, quitting
the mountain's frozen


ridge, gathering your grey mass: heavy
slow clouds massed on darkening banks
and poured you down through the standing air
across the cracked bed


from summit: they emptied in a season;
and you, patient one, a gleam
on your unhurried surface, asked me
what was the drought now, and why


was I so parched now, and what
did I most need to swallow
in my splitting clay: "Which slope
should Gravity now tilt


toward your thirst? Who dammed you,
Riverbed? For even if it climbs,
soon it will fall again; if it withholds
its flood, soon it will release it;

spatial_form.notes: Five quatrains separated by blank lines; enjambment carries syntax across stanza boundaries (lines 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17). A quoted voice opens mid-final-quatrains and continues into the last stanza.

coherence_axes: petition addressed upward to a returning power
the one-directional descent of aid (from above, toward the caller)
the reversal-formula in which flight becomes pursuit, refusal becomes giving
layer_b_declaration.semantic_field: hydrology / a dry riverbed petitioning the returning rains and the water's downhill obedience

rotation.commentary: The source's gesture is one-directional: aid descends, the god comes down, and the reversal-formula (flight→pursuit, refusal→gift) all point one way — toward the caller's restoration. MIRROR takes the directionality-axis and lets the descent's symmetry surface: water obeys gravity, but the operator names the wager as the reciprocity the original foreclosed — what falls must climb to fall again. The counter-motion tercet ("even if it climbs, / soon it will fall again; if it withholds / its flood, soon it will release it") holds the same conditional cadence as Sappho's flight/pursuit formula while enacting the cyclical return the human petition could only imagine as one-time rescue. The five-quatrain geometry, the four cross-stanza enjambments, the mid-quatrain opening of a quoted voice, and the double-address (the named caller answered by name) all map unit-by-unit. Semantic field is hydrological, disjoint from erotic-divine petition; Aphrodite, sparrows, chariot, Persuasion leave no trace. Source is not reconstructable from clouds and cracked bed. The witness's question — will there be a return on what was broken — is answered by the axis itself: the mirror discloses that descent implies ascent, that the broken (dry) bed's petition is structurally guaranteed a return, because the water that fell must rise to fall again. Cost is legible: the return is real but cyclic, not the once-and-for-all rescue the caller wanted.

rotation.enantiomorph:
but turn to me, if once in the past
you caught my low signal-fires
and answered, and rose, quitting
the deep bar's silver


bed, hauling your long swell: bright
foam hissed along the running crests
and bore you inward through the narrowed strait
across the drowned flats


from open sea: you crested in a breath;
and you, patient one, a churn
on your unweathered brow, asked me
what was the trouble now, and why


was I flaring now, and what
did I most need dragged up
from my capsized hold: "Whose keel
should the Undertow bring


back to your moorage? Who has grounded you,
harborman? For even if she drifts,
soon she will steer home; if she spurns
the hawser, soon she will take it;

beat_map: conditional summons anchored in remembered heeding
the departure and yoking — motion begins
descent and instant arrival across the distances
the addressed one's inquiry into the cause of the call
reported speech: the reversal-promise begun as catalogue

spatial_form.notes: Five quatrains, no indentation; enjambment carries syntax across stanza boundaries (stanza 1->2, 3->4, 4->5); a colon opens quoted speech mid-stanza-4 and the reported voice runs into stanza 5; the final line ends mid-catalogue on a semicolon (open, unclosed).

coherence_axes: invocation-as-recall (the plea grounded in prior answered pleas)
traversal of a vast interval collapsed to immediacy
a superior addressed presence questioning the supplicant's need
reversal promised through inventory of what will turn
layer_b_declaration.semantic_field: a shipwright / harbormaster petitioning the tide itself to return a lost hull; maritime salvage and tidal reversal

rotation.commentary: The source is a hymn-of-recall: a plea that draws its force from a prior answering, a divine descent collapsing distance to instantness, a questioning by the summoned power, and a reversal-catalogue left grammatically open. The SHADOW operator, on the assertion-axis, receives the bearing-cost the composer underwent — the wager that calling again presumes on a love already spent, that the reversal is promised but the sentence never closes. The enantiomorph relocates this into tidal salvage: a harborman flaring signal-fires to the Undertow that once returned a hull, the sea's inward traversal across drowned flats, the power's inquiry ("Whose keel...who has grounded you"), and the same unclosed catalogue of turnings (drifts→steers home, spurns→takes the hawser) breaking off on a semicolon. Five quatrains, no indent, the identical enjambment pattern and the final open semicolon reproduce the spatial skeleton. The cost is legible: the return is asserted (she will pursue, she will give / she will steer, she will take) yet the syntax refuses to seal it — the question "will there be a return on what was broken" is answered only as a promise still mid-inventory, never landed.
